hints: Use the generalized binomial expansion on $(1+6x)^{-1/3}$.
Simplify each coefficient and retain terms through $x^3$.
walkthrough:
Rewrite the given algebraic expression using a negative fractional exponent:
$$\dfrac{1}{\sqrt[3]{1 + 6x}} = (1 + 6x)^{-1/3}$$

Recall the generalized binomial expansion formula for $(1 + u)^n$ where $n$ is rational and $|u| < 1$:
$$(1 + u)^n = 1 + nu + \dfrac{n(n - 1)}{2!}u^2 + \dfrac{n(n - 1)(n - 2)}{3!}u^3 + \cdots$$
Identify the parameters for this expansion: $n = -\dfrac{1}{3}$ and $u = 6x$.

Calculate the quadratic coefficient and term ($x^2$ term):
$$\dfrac{n(n - 1)}{2!} = \dfrac{\left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\right)\left(-\dfrac{1}{3} - 1\right)}{2} = \dfrac{\left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\right)\left(-\dfrac{4}{3}\right)}{2} = \dfrac{\dfrac{4}{9}}{2} = \dfrac{2}{9}$$
$$\dfrac{n(n - 1)}{2!}u^2 = \dfrac{2}{9}(6x)^2 = \dfrac{2}{9}(36x^2) = 2(4x^2) = 8x^2$$

Calculate the cubic coefficient and term ($x^3$ term):
$$\dfrac{n(n - 1)(n - 2)}{3!} = \dfrac{\left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\right)\left(-\dfrac{4}{3}\right)\left(-\dfrac{1}{3} - 2\right)}{6} = \dfrac{\left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\right)\left(-\dfrac{4}{3}\right)\left(-\dfrac{7}{3}\right)}{6} = \dfrac{-\dfrac{28}{27}}{6} = -\dfrac{28}{162} = -\dfrac{14}{81}$$
$$\dfrac{n(n - 1)(n - 2)}{3!}u^3 = -\dfrac{14}{81}(6x)^3 = -\dfrac{14}{81}(216x^3)$$
Simplify by dividing $216$ and $81$ by their greatest common divisor $27$:
$$\dfrac{216}{27} = 8, \quad \dfrac{81}{27} = 3 \implies -\dfrac{14 \times 8}{3}x^3 = -\dfrac{112}{3}x^3$$

Combine all terms in ascending powers of $x$ up to $x^3$:
$$(1 + 6x)^{-1/3} = 1 - 2x + 8x^2 - \dfrac{112}{3}x^3 + \cdots$$

ai_rubric.Binomial Expansion: Gives an unsimplified version of the $x$ or $x^2$ or $x^3$ term in the expansion of $(1+6x)^{-1/3}$. Gives first two terms $1-2x$. The final result is $1-2x+8x^2-\frac{112}{3}x^3$.
